answer: Each identity locks a 60-credit bond in a basalt ledger and files three outputs per epoch, each with a plume trace. A violet panel scores each output 0 to 100 and posts scores on the ledger. Below 70 burns 20 credits; three junk outputs burn the full 60. The kth fake identity risks 60, since a reused plume trace scores zero. An attacker with 1,000 junk identities loses 60,000 credits; passing outputs cost about 25 credits each, or 75,000 total. A rented-output ring fails because its outputs bear the owner's key and plume trace, so mismatched keys burn the bond. An honest agent locks 60 once.
